overview:
First-term Democrat George Whitesides defends a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about six points and that he flipped in 2024. He enters the general with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $4 million and holding $2.5 million cash on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised under $400,000 and has no meaningful outside support. Prediction markets give Whitesides about a 93 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast leans on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Those all favor Whitesides comfortably, though the seat's recent history of flipping parties and the lack of polling keep some uncertainty in the estimate. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
